channel.title: Another Day for the (Logistics Department)
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Another Day for the (Logistics Department)" - Gabriel's day transferring a regular item to another site. Regular for the Foundation anyways...

item.title: Re: Another Day for the (Logistics Department)
item.content:encoded:
In case you come back to see this reply:

You are most certainly correct. As for what this basic plot will do:

  • Introduce Gabriel (A character I may have for future tales)
  • GOI Building: I want to build on how the GOI operates (CI). At least, how they carry out their missions. So far, we have an idea how they work, but I've only seen a handful of tales in action.
  • The SCP will either be A. selected from a pre-existing SCP or B. Be an SCP I was hoping to work on. I would prefer A, but we'll see how that works.
  • Most Importantly: I want to show the inner workings of the Logistics Department. Routes, assignments, so on and so forth. The Action/Horror is just a way to get invested in the boring delivery job. Also showing that while it's usually boring, there is still risk in being in this sort of job. Any Foundation job is dangerous. I just want to show WHY this one is dangerous.

item.title: Re: Another Day for the (Logistics Department)
item.content:encoded:
Hiya. Disclaimer: I am not authorized to give greenlights. please reach out to more experienced users for more informed crit.

To summarize, I think this is a (potentially) good premise, and a bad pitch.

The summary you've laid out is really just a basic thriller set-up. Everyman dude has a thing, bad things happen, dude has to get from point A to point B with the thing. This is the elemental premise of most western action-thrillers, so it doesn't give me any insight into the potential appeal of such a tale. With such a basic plot structure, the reader will most likely not be taken in by the premise alone, and so you're going to have to rely on other elements of your writing toolbox to generate interest.

That being said, having a common plot structure is not at all a bad thing! Execution is everything. It's just that it's hard for me to tell from the info you've provided what the angle of that execution is. Will Gabriel's character development invest the reader? Does the unknown anomaly have fascinating or confusing effects that will warp the story in an interesting way? Is there a conspiracy going on with the GOI that sets up some chilling world-building opportunities?

It's not that this idea can't or won't work, it's just that the info you've provided doesn't sell me.

Have a good day!

item.title: Another Day for the (Logistics Department)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Horror, Comedy, Action,

Page Layout (Optional): N/A

Elevator Pitch: Courier Gabriel travels to deliver an unknown SCP to Site-19 with complications along the way.

Central Narrative: Gabriel starts off loading the SCP into his delivery truck, noting not to ask questions on what's inside. Everything goes smoothly (agents with him), until they are attacked by an unknown GOI. The agents are lost or killed and Gabriel must finish this one-day delivery with guns pointed at him in every direction with the added fact that an unknown SCP is inside and he has no idea what it does.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: No one has really written about the Logistics Department. I hope to start with these guys and do a series of each department, small and big. All of them will have a tad of workplace comedy, danger, and horror to whatever they're dealing with. It's Ironic how "Another Day" in the Foundation can usually mean life or death, no matter who you are.

Additional Notes: Ask me anything, I'll answer. I always love to hear a good crit about how to improve. Be blunt. Bash as hard as you can. You'll find I have a thick skull.
